verdict.rationale: Bitwarden's official CLI can be authenticated non-interactively with a personal API key for automated workflows. Its `bw serve` mode exposes the vault as a local REST API that an agent can query for TOTP codes. A hands-on user report independently confirms the CLI outputs current TOTP codes, and the integrated authenticator generates the rotating 30-second codes. Missing for 10: a first-party doc quote showing the specific TOTP retrieval command or endpoint, and documentation of an end-to-end automated 2FA login flow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can fetch a current TOTP code programmatically — via CLI or API — to complete a 2FA login inside an automated workflow

citations.quote: the CLI whose documented `bw serve` mode exposes the whole vault as a local RESTful API (Vault Management API) an agent can query for TOTP codes and items
it listed everything including passwords and current totp codes in plaintext
Using the personal API key for CLI authentication is suitable for automated workflows
it automatically produces the time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs), six-digit codes using SHA-1 that rotate every 30 seconds
